title: Climate Change Could Wipe Out Japan's Ski Resorts
paragraphs: Japan is famous for its powder snow, and every winter, skiers from Japan and around the world visit its ski resorts. However, a new study warns that climate change could force most of these resorts to close.

The study was carried out by researchers from Hokkaido University and the Forestry and Forest Products Research Institute in Tsukuba, Ibaraki Prefecture. The results were announced in September 2026. The researchers looked at 349 ski areas across Japan that have lifts or gondolas.

The researchers used climate data to predict how much natural snow each ski area would get in the future. They said a ski area could operate if it could offer skiing for at least 100 days a year without using artificial snow.

The researchers looked at two possible futures. In the first, the world's average temperature rises by 2 degrees Celsius compared with the time before industrialization. This matches the goal of the Paris Agreement, an international agreement on climate change. In this case, 53 ski areas could operate fully and 108 could operate partly.

In the second, the temperature rises by 4 degrees. This could happen if the world does very little to stop climate change. In this case, only seven ski areas could operate fully. They are in Hokkaido and in the Akita, Yamagata, Gunma and Nagano prefectures. Another 26 could operate partly.
The researchers found that ski areas that are higher up or farther north are more likely to survive.
According to reports, a big drop in the number of ski areas could seriously harm Japan's ski culture and the economies of towns that depend on winter tourism.
